messages:
Alex M: Heads up — spotted a sharp spike in provisional token counts for customer `acme` during the canary. Console shows a big provisional bar then a smaller final charge.
Maya R: Logs: https://internal/logs/trace/abcd1234 — looks correlated with a wave of reconnects and retry attempts.
Chris G: My reading: inflight retries + streaming truncation + toolcall fallback = double/ambiguous charging window. Client reconnects -> router replays -> toolcall happens on the second path.
Jun K: Current billing flow: we emit provisional tokens at stream start, finalize on stream end (or toolcall resolution). Retries aren't deduped unless there's an explicit idempotency key.
Sarah L: Proposal: router should attach a cross-phase idempotency token `x-rw-inflight-id` and carry it through stream -> toolcall -> finalization. Persist mapping for short TTL so retries can dedupe.
Alex M: Example header we'd like:
```
X-RW-Inflight-Id: cust123:req9876
X-RW-Attempt: 1
```
Maya R: Problem: many clients don't set attempt metadata. Router-generated ids must be stable across reconnects from the same client session or we won't dedupe.
Chris G: Short-term mitigation idea: treat immediate reconnect (<2s) from same src ip + same connection metadata as the same inflight and suppress provisional increment.
Jun K: Also need stronger telemetry: tag billing events with `billing_reason` (stream_start|stream_final|toolcall_fallback|retry) and include `inflight_id`. That will help reconcile UI spikes.
Sarah L: Console UX change request: show provisional vs final token counts per request in the request details panel, with a "pending" state and hover tooltip explaining provisional billing. That should reduce support tickets.
Alex M: Edge case: server-side truncation to fit max_tokens can change the prompt that triggers a toolcall. We currently sometimes end up charging both the truncated stream and the toolcall payload because they look like different requests.
Maya R: For Dedicated customers with strict quotas, this causes false quota exhaustion alerts. Need a non-invasive short-term patch.
Jun K: Minimum viable quick fix: router keeps an in-memory inflight map (falling back to Redis) keyed by `client_session_id|req_id` with TTL 60s. Before emitting provisional tokens, check map. If key exists and is marked "inflight_retry", skip provisional increment and mark the event as retry in telemetry.
Chris G: Long-term: persist inflight mapping in Redis with CAS to avoid racey increments under surge. Also add reconciler job that looks for provisional entries older than X and auto-finalizes or flags for human review.
ops-bot: deploy note — billing-router patch queued for canary: 2026-03-19T15:20Z; prometheus rule `billing.provisional_ratio` added to watch.
Maya R: Agree on short-term Redis map + better tags. I'll mock the console panels for provisional vs final (small badge + timeline).
Sarah L: Also need a migration plan for older in-flight identifiers for Dedicated — we'll need a compatibility layer for customers with proxying.
Chris G: Can we expose a finalization webhook customers can subscribe to so they get notified when provisional charges clear into final? Could reduce support noise.
Alex M: +1. I'll draft an RFC for the router idempotency change (inflight-store design, fields, TTL, collision policy, rollout canary). Will include metrics to track: `billing.provisional_vs_final_ratio`, `billing.retry_dedupe_rate`, and `inflight.map_collision_rate`.
Maya R: I'll produce console mockups and help define the event schema for telemetry.
Jun K: I'll instrument the metrics and add a Grafana panel for canary monitoring.
Chris G: QA will need a test harness that simulates reconnects, truncation + toolcall fallback to validate dedupe.
Sarah L: Assignments: Alex RFC, Maya console mock, Jun metrics + dashboard, Chris QA tests.
Alex M: ETA: RFC by EOD tomorrow, canary target next week. :thumbsup:
